institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Institute of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Clinical Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 28, No. 1: percentage sensitivity, January to December 2021. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published May 2022.
reporting: Percent susceptible by specimen (blood, urine, pus/tissue, body fluids, respiratory specimens), organism (Gram-positive and Gram-negative tables) and location (OPD, ward, ICU), with the number of isolates per row; organism counts per specimen and location in bar charts with printed data labels and an "others" list.
method: MIC testing on Vitek 2, interpreted with CLSI 2021 guidelines; repeat isolates excluded (printed in parentheses).

verification.note: All 10 susceptibility tables (GPC and GNB, pages 2 to 6) were parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber word positions; column headers rebuilt from the rotated header text; OPD, ward and ICU taken from each row's background colour and checked against the row order), then every cell and every row n was compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 4 and cropped into left and right halves: no differences, except that the urine GPC Glycopeptides column, printed half a row below its rows, was not parsed and was read from the page and the text layer (assigned in order, see notes), and that the pus GNB Tigecycline and body fluid GNB Minocycline columns were read but not recorded (see excluded). Organism charts: bar data labels were matched to the legend swatches by colour and legend order and the "others" lists parsed from the text layer; every panel (bars, legend and others list) was then compared by eye with the chart rendered at scale 4 and checked arithmetically (named bars plus Others equal the printed isolates; the others list sums to Others), and every table n was compared with the chart count of the same organism, specimen and location: all 15 panels balance and all agree. Read from the image because the parse failed: the three blood Others bars (179, 219 and 212, labels printed inside the top of tall bars) and the three blood others lists (first line lost and names split by the parser; transcribed in full from the image), the bars of urine ICU, pus OPD (15 bars), the three body fluid panels and respiratory OPD, the body fluid ward others list (first line lost), the pus OPD entry "Strept. pneumoniae-3" (split over two lines) and the respiratory ward and ICU legend "Stenotrophomonas maltophilia" (split over two lines). The six cells the build does not keep were re-read on the page and are printed as recorded.

notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 28, No. 1 (published May 2022), data January to December 2021, 8 pages. The PDF has no direct link: sgrh.com serves it only by an HTTP POST from the Microbiology Newsletter selector on https://sgrh.com/en/publications (issue "May-2022"; the file downloads as mb-may2022.pdf). Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus/tissue; body fluids; respiratory specimens): organism bar charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates with the repeat isolates excluded in parentheses, a data label on every bar and an "others" list) and Gram-positive (GPC) and Gram-negative (GNB) percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus (printed "Pus / Tissue", pus and tissue reported together), sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory. Coagulase-negative staphylococci: the blood GPC row is printed "Staphylococcus spp.#" with the footnote "#Break up of Staphylcoccus spp: S.haemolyticus: 71, S. epidermidis: 87, S. hominis: 58, S.capitis: 8, Other Staph. spp. 5" (229, the sum of the three rows), and the pus row "Staphylococci spp."; both are recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci, as the 2011 edition labels the same row "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)". Enterococci are reported by species (printed "Enterococci faecium" and "Enterococci faecalis", recorded as E. faecium and E. faecalis). Combined columns: "Cefoxitin/Oxacillin" is recorded under oxacillin, "Imipenem/ Meropenem" (every GNB table) under meropenem and "Glycopeptides" under vancomycin (vancomycin and teicoplanin reported as one figure), each cell noted. The blood GNB column is headed "*Imipenem/ Meropenem" with the footnote advising an alternative method of testing before reporting Vitek 2 imipenem results for Proteus, Morganella and Providencia (none has a blood row). The urine and pus pages print "*Sensitivity of Meropenem given" although no cell or header of those tables carries an asterisk. "Co-Amoxyclav" is recorded under amoxiclav. The "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded. Colistin is not reported (no colistin column; this edition gives no reason, the 2020 edition states that CLSI has had no susceptible category for colistin in Gram-negative bacteria since 2020). The respiratory GNB table adds Stenotrophomonas maltophilia rows; in that table cefepime equals ceftazidime in every P. aeruginosa and S. maltophilia row (recorded as printed). Layout problems: (1) the urine GPC Glycopeptides column is printed about half a row below its row bands (each value between two rows, the last "-" below the table border); its six entries 61, 67, 56, 90, -, - are assigned in order to E. faecium OPD, ward, ICU and E. faecalis OPD, ward, ICU, the only reading that places every entry in a row and the one that matches the "-" of the E. faecalis ward and ICU rows; each such cell says so. (2) The pus GNB Tigecycline column repeats the Imipenem/Meropenem column value for value in all 14 printed rows, including Proteus (94, 93, 100) and P. aeruginosa (67, 63, 71); it is not recorded. (3) The body fluid GNB Minocycline column has two series printed over each other and cannot be read; not recorded. Both are listed in excluded. Isolate numbers: every table n equals the chart count of the same organism, specimen and location, and every chart panel balances (named bars plus Others equal the printed isolates; the "others" list sums to Others). The blood "others" lists begin with "CONS" (OPD 104, ward 122, ICU 127) beside the Staphylococcus spp. bars (59, 79, 91, equal to the table n), and the body fluid OPD list prints "Cons-2" beside "Staphylococcus spp. -2"; the CONS entries are not recorded (see excluded). Per-drug tested numbers are not printed: 62 of the 779 recorded percentages are not k/n of the row's n (11 of them fit truncation). Two can be given by no number of tested isolates up to the row's n (pus ICU E. faecium high-dose gentamicin 6 with n = 14; pus ward E. faecalis high-dose gentamicin 36 with n = 10): recorded as printed with conflict entries. The build also treats as intrinsic resistance urine Enterobacter co-amoxyclav 6 (OPD) and 10 (ward), respiratory ICU P. aeruginosa ceftriaxone 0 and respiratory ICU A. baumannii ertapenem 0; all printed that way. Organism counts: every bar and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla", "Serratia marscecens", "S. maltophila", "L.monocytogenes"); "Salmonella typhimurium" is recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella and "Burkholderia vietnamiensis" as Burkholderia spp. Fungi: "Fungal isolates" (not recordable); species recorded under their keys only in panels with no unnamed fungal entry (body fluid ICU Candida albicans 12 and Aspergillus fumigatus 1; respiratory OPD Aspergillus fumigatus 12, A. flavus 7 and A. niger 1); blood ward Candida auris 18 and Candida tropicalis 11 and urine OPD Trichosporon asahii 6 sit beside a "Fungal isolates" entry in the same panel, are a partial count and are listed in excluded; their susceptibility data were deferred to the next issue. Entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. Page 1 (case report: XDR Salmonella Typhi), page 7 (prescription auditing of antimicrobials and the drug resistance index) and page 8 (case report continued, publications, highlights) carry no susceptibility tables.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 779 cells (the seeded 25% sample of 195 from sample_cells.py, spread over all 10 GPC and GNB tables on pages 2 to 6, plus every other cell), all 91 row n values, the 20 printed table rows not recorded and all 251 organism counts were read from the page images (tables at scale 3 cut into halves with the row labels and n kept, the urine GPC table at scale 6; the 15 chart panels at scale 4) and checked against an independent word-position parse of the text layer that takes OPD, ward and ICU from each cell's own fill colour: image and parse agree on all 111 printed table rows apart from the urine GPC Glycopeptides column below.

Result: 0 transcription errors; no value, n or count changed. OPD, ward and ICU correct on every row (yellow, blue and pink fills, in that order in every triple of every table); the organism label of every row triple and the specimen of every page correct (pus GPC lists Staph. aureus before Staphylococci spp.; body fluid GNB lists Klebsiella before E. coli); every printed value of a recorded column is in the file and nothing else is; the 20 rows not recorded are exactly the rows printed all "-", as excluded says. No table reached the 2% error threshold.

Urine GPC Glycopeptides: the whole column, header included, is printed about 7 pt (0.7 of a row) low, so 61, 67, 56, 90 and "-" each straddle two row bands and the last "-" sits below the table border. The order reading in the file (E. faecium OPD 61, ward 67, ICU 56; E. faecalis OPD 90, ward and ICU "-") is agreed: it is the only reading that puts one entry in each of the six rows, whereas reading by position would leave E. faecium OPD empty, put an entry outside the table and give the E. faecalis ward row (all "-" elsewhere) a value.

Excluded columns confirmed: the pus GNB Tigecycline column repeats Imipenem/Meropenem in all 14 printed rows (including Proteus 94, 93, 100 and P. aeruginosa 67, 63, 71); the body fluid GNB Minocycline column prints two series over each other in every cell and cannot be read on the page (the text layer holds one series identical to Imipenem/Meropenem and another, 33, 14, 23, 25, 25, 63, -, -, -). Both rightly not recorded. No other overprinted text on pages 2 to 6 of the 2019, 2020 or 2021 editions.

Columns: all 13 Cefoxitin/Oxacillin cells (under oxacillin), all 55 Imipenem/Meropenem cells (10 blood "*Imipenem/ Meropenem", 45 others; under meropenem) and all 27 Glycopeptides cells (under vancomycin) carry their cell note; Co-Amoxyclav under amoxiclav; Quinolones not recorded. Footnotes confirmed: "#Break up of Staphylcoccus spp: S.haemolyticus: 71, S. epidermidis: 87, S. hominis: 58, S.capitis: 8, Other Staph. spp. 5" (229 = 59 + 79 + 91); the blood "*" note on Vitek 2 imipenem for Proteus, Morganella and Providencia; "*Sensitivity of Meropenem given" printed on the urine and pus pages with no asterisk in those tables.

Charts: all 15 panels balance on the image (blood ward others list read from the image, its "Brevundimonas sps.2" has no hyphen); bar order equals legend order in every panel; all 111 table n equal their chart count; the 251 counts are exactly the recordable bar and others entries, the rest named in excluded. The blood "CONS" entries (OPD 104, ward 122, ICU "Cons-127") and body fluid OPD "Cons-2" are printed in the others lists beside the "Staphylococcus spp." bars (blood 59, 79, 91, equal to the table n and to the footnote break-up of coagulase-negative species): leaving them out of counts, as the file does, keeps the CoNS count equal to the tabulated rows; the ICU Cons-127 equals the Fungal Isolates bar 127, printed that way.

Cells the build does not keep, re-read: urine Enterobacter co-amoxyclav 6 (OPD) and 10 (ward), respiratory ICU P. aeruginosa ceftriaxone 0 and A. baumannii ertapenem 0, pus ICU E. faecium high-dose gentamicin 6 (n = 14) and pus ward E. faecalis high-dose gentamicin 36 (n = 10) are all printed that way; the two conflict entries are correct (no whole number of tested isolates up to n gives 6 or 36).

Lead 2026-09-26: fungal chart entries follow one rule across the SGRH editions: recorded as counts unless the same panel also prints an unnamed fungal entry (then a partial count, excluded): moved to excluded: blood ward Candida auris 18; blood ward Candida tropicalis 11; urine opd Trichosporon asahii 6.
